questions.question: A statement is given followed by two conclusions. Find which conclusion is TRUE based on the given statement. Statement: C ≥ T ; A = D ≥ O ; G ≥ D < S ; T ≥ A Conclusions: I: A ≤ O II: C ≥ G
questions.questionHtml:
A statement is given followed by two conclusions. Find which conclusion is TRUE based on the given statement.

Statement:

C ≥ T ; A = D ≥ O ; G ≥ D < S ; T ≥ A

Conclusions:

I: A ≤ O

II: C ≥ G
questions.solution:
I. A ≤ O → False (From A = D ≥ O, we get A ≥ O, so A ≤ O is incorrect.)

II. C ≥ G → False (From C ≥ T ≥ A = D and G ≥ D, no definite relation can be established between C and G.)

Thus, Neither I nor II follows.

∴ The correct answer is "Option 4".

questions.question: Read the following statement carefully and identify the conclusion that follows. Statement: All citizens must abide by traffic laws. Conclusion I: Citizens who disobey traffic laws must be punished. Conclusion II: Obeying traffic laws shows civic responsibility.
questions.questionHtml:
Read the following statement carefully and identify the conclusion that follows.

Statement: All citizens must abide by traffic laws.

Conclusion I: Citizens who disobey traffic laws must be punished.

Conclusion II: Obeying traffic laws shows civic responsibility.
questions.solution:
I. Citizens who disobey traffic laws must be punished – True (If citizens are required to follow traffic laws, those who violate them are expected to face punishment.)

II. Obeying traffic laws shows civic responsibility – True (Following traffic rules reflects responsible behavior as a citizen.)

Thus, Both conclusions follow.

questions.question: Instruction: Identify the assumptions that must hold for the statement to be valid, then choose the correct option. Statement: To reduce traffic congestion in urban areas, cities should invest in public transportation infrastructure, even though it requires significant initial investments. Assumptions: I. Public transportation can effectively reduce traffic congestion. II. The initial cost of building transportation infrastructure is high. III. People are willing to shift from private vehicles to public transportation.
questions.questionHtml:
Instruction: Identify the assumptions that must hold for the statement to be valid, then choose the correct option.

Statement: To reduce traffic congestion in urban areas, cities should invest in public transportation infrastructure, even though it requires significant initial investments.

Assumptions:

I. Public transportation can effectively reduce traffic congestion.

II. The initial cost of building transportation infrastructure is high.

III. People are willing to shift from private vehicles to public transportation.

options.text: Only I and II are implicit
options.html: Only I and II are implicit

options.text: Only II and III are implicit
options.html: Only II and III are implicit

options.text: All I, II and III are implicit
options.html: All I, II and III are implicit

questions.solution:
I. Public transportation can effectively reduce traffic congestion – True (The statement suggests investing in public transport to reduce congestion, so it assumes public transport can help reduce traffic.)

II. The initial cost of building transportation infrastructure is high – True (The statement clearly mentions that it requires significant initial investments.)

III. People are willing to shift from private vehicles to public transportation – False (The statement does not necessarily assume people are willing to shift; it only suggests investment in infrastructure.)

Thus, Only I and II are implicit.

questions.question: Read the following statement carefully and identify the conclusion that follows. Statement: Thousands of students appeared for the entrance exam conducted across the country. Conclusions: I. The exam is popular and competitive. II. All students who appeared will get admission.
questions.questionHtml:
Read the following statement carefully and identify the conclusion that follows.

Statement: Thousands of students appeared for the entrance exam conducted across the country.

Conclusions:

I. The exam is popular and competitive.

II. All students who appeared will get admission.
questions.solution:
I. The exam is popular and competitive – True (Since thousands of students appeared for the exam, it indicates that the exam is popular and likely competitive.)

II. All students who appeared will get admission – False (The statement does not say that all students will get admission; entrance exams usually select only some candidates.)

Hence, Only Conclusion I follows.

∴ The correct answer is "Option 1".

questions.question: Read the following statement carefully and identify the conclusion that follows. Statement: All circles are shapes. Some shapes are squares. All squares are polygons. Conclusions: I. Some shapes are polygons. II. Some polygons are circles.
questions.questionHtml:
Read the following statement carefully and identify the conclusion that follows.

Statement:

All circles are shapes. Some shapes are squares. All squares are polygons.

Conclusions:

I. Some shapes are polygons.

II. Some polygons are circles.
questions.solution:
I. Some shapes are polygons – True (Since some shapes are squares and all squares are polygons, therefore those shapes which are squares are also polygons.)

II. Some polygons are circles – False (No definite relation is given between polygons and circles, so this cannot be concluded.)

Thus, Only Conclusion I follows.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".

questions.question: A boat travels 60 kilometers upstream in 3 hours and covers the same distance of 60 kilometers downstream in 2 hours. What is the speed of the boat in still water?
questions.questionHtml: A boat travels 60 kilometers upstream in 3 hours and covers the same distance of 60 kilometers downstream in 2 hours. What is the speed of the boat in still water?
questions.solution:
Speed of boat in still water = (Upstream speed + Downstream speed) / 2

Calculation:

Upstream speed = 60 / 3 = 20 km/h

Downstream speed = 60 / 2 = 30 km/h

Speed of boat in still water = (20 + 30) / 2

= 50 / 2 = 25 km/h

questions.question: The series given below contains a sequence of numbers. Accordingly identify the incorrect combination 4, 5, 14, 14, 34, 36, 74, 68
questions.questionHtml: The series given below contains a sequence of numbers. Accordingly identify the incorrect combination 4, 5, 14, 14, 34, 36, 74, 68
questions.solution:
Odd position numbers follow: ×2 + increasing even numbers

4 × 2 + 6 = 14 , 14 × 2 + 6 = 34 , 34 × 2 + 6 = 74

Odd position series: 4, 14, 34, 74 ✔

Even position numbers follow: ×2 + increasing even numbers

5 × 2 + 4 = 14 , 14 × 2 + 4 = 32 , 32 × 2 + 4 = 68

Expected even series: 5, 14, 32, 68

Given even series: 5, 14, 36, 68
